newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-LATE MILOSEVIC GOAL FLOORS CZECHS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE MILOSEVIC GOAL FLOORS CZECHS.

text.p: Substitute Savo Milosevic all but ended the Czech Republic's hopes of a berth in the 1998 World Cup finals when he scored in the final minute to lift Yugoslavia to a 2-1 victory in their European group six qualifier on Wednesday.
Milosevic, who came on for AC Milan's Dejan Savicevic in the 82nd minute, took a perfect cross from Ljubinko Drulovic, another late substitute, to give the outplayed Yugoslavs the three points.

The Czechs, beaten Euro 96 finalists, dominated from the opening whistle but failed to find the scoring touch that has deserted them since they opened their qualifying programme with a 6-0 drubbing of Malta.
Their only goal came from Atletico Madrid's Radek Bejbl in the 75th minute. Predrag Mijatovic's free kick had given Yugoslavia the lead in the 28th minute.
The Czechs have taken just four points from four games. Leaders Spain have 16 from six, Yugoslavia 15 from six and Slovakia 12 from five.
